terms.meaning: a reusable building block of a screen, such as a menu or button, that can be placed in many places
a library of unstyled, accessible menu and dialog parts that handle behavior, leaving the look to the app
short style words placed in a component's class setting, such as those controlling padding, color, or size
a way to pass a direct handle to the underlying element so other code can reach it
settings passed into a component by the code that uses it
a way to draw content in a separate layer above the page so it is not cut off by its parent
a menu that opens from another menu item
a readable label for a component, shown in developer tools when debugging

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Imports and base menu parts
sections.what: Brings in the menu library, icons, and style helper, then gives the base menu parts short names this file can reuse. Nothing is shown on screen yet.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets up the base parts that every wrapper below builds on.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Main menu box and clickable rows
sections.what: Builds the floating box that appears on right-click and the rows inside it. The box stops at a height limit and scrolls when it has many entries. Rows highlight when focused and dim when disabled. Checkbox rows are also set up here.
sections.why: Likely reason: applies the shared look to the main box and to the rows users click.
sections.watch_out: The height limit depends on a value the library supplies, so removing it can break scrolling.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Radio options, labels, and dividers
sections.what: Builds radio options that show a filled dot when chosen, group label text, and the thin line that separates groups of entries.
sections.why: Likely reason: visually groups and marks the entries in a menu.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Shortcut hint text and exports
sections.what: Builds the small grey text on the right side of a row that shows a keyboard shortcut. It only displays text; it does not register any shortcut. The final list makes all these parts available to other files.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows users which key combination runs an action. The code only shows the text.
sections.watch_out: The hint is display only, so the real shortcut must be wired up somewhere else.

summary: Builds the styled pieces of a right-click menu (the menu box, clickable rows, checkboxes, radio options, labels, dividers, submenus, and shortcut hint text) on top of a third-party menu library.
purpose: Gives every right-click menu in the app the same look. Other screens import these pieces and assemble them. This file adds styling only. Opening, closing, and keyboard navigation come from the underlying library.
why: Likely reason: these wrappers follow a common shared component pattern, so every menu looks the same. The code does not state this directly.
how: It imports the base menu library, an icon set, and a small helper that merges style strings. It gives each base part a ContextMenu name, then wraps the parts that need styling. Those include the main box, rows, checkboxes, radio options, labels, dividers, submenu parts, and shortcut text. It then lists all of them as exports so other files can use them.
inputs: Settings passed in by the screen that uses the menu: optional style overrides, an indent flag on some rows, the checked state on checkboxes, and standard element settings.
outputs: Ready-made menu components that other screens place inside a right-click area. Nothing is saved or stored.
risks: Nothing here is destructive. The main risk is visual: changing a style string can make menus look wrong or lose hover highlighting. Keyboard and focus behavior depend on the underlying library.
debug: If a right-click menu does not open, check the screen that wraps the clickable area, not this file. If styling looks wrong, check the style strings in the matching wrapper here. Some long style strings were cut off in the copy I was given, so I could not check them in full.
